extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, IPEA staff, and patent applicants/agents involved in PCT Chapter II (international preliminary examination) proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for processing PCT Chapter II (international preliminary) examinations including handling of Article 19/34 amendments, timing and docketing rules, unity of invention practice, rectification of mistakes, forms, telephonic practice, and protest procedures. Targets actions by examiners and expectations for applicants/agents filing amendments and replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sheets and letter for amended description/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: When amendments to the description or drawings are made under PCT Rule 66.8, the applicant shall be required to submit a replacement sheet for every sheet of the international application which, on account of an amendment, differs from the sheet previously filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The replacement sheet(s) shall be accompanied by a letter which shall draw attention to the differences between the replaced sheets and the replacement sheets, shall indicate the basis for the amendment in the application as filed and shall preferably also explain the reasons for the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement sheets and letter for amended claims (complete set)
rubrics_metrics.description: When amendments to the claims are made under PCT Rule 66.8, the applicant shall be required to submit a replacement sheet or sheets containing a complete set of claims in replacement of all the claims originally filed or previously amended under Articles 19 or 34.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The replacement sheet(s) must be accompanied by a letter that (A) identifies the claims which, on account of the amendments, differ from the claims originally filed, (B) identify the claims originally filed which, on account of the amendments, are cancelled, and (C) indicate the basis for the amendments in the application as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Article 19 amendments are claim-only and post-search
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 19 amendments are exclusively amendments to the claims and these amendments can only be made after the international search report has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 19 amendments, any statement referred to in that Article, and the letter required under PCT Rule 46.5(b) will be transmitted to the IPEA by the IB unless the IPEA indicates it already received such a copy. The IB marks replacement sheets submitted under PCT Article 19 with the international application number, receipt date and the words 'AMENDED SHEET (ARTICLE 19).' If a copy of Article 19 amendments has not been stamped by the IB, the IPEA/US will treat the unstamped copy as an amendment under PCT Article 34.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments must not add new matter or introduce obscurity
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment must not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment must not add subject matter which goes beyond the disclosure of the international application as originally filed. Furthermore, it should not itself cause the international application as amended to be objectionable under the PCT, e.g., the amendment should not introduce obscurity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents required before IPEA starts international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA starts the international preliminary examination when it is in possession of the demand; the required fees; if a translation is required, that translation; either the international search report or a notice that no ISR will be established; and the written opinion established under PCT Rule 43bis.1, unless the applicant expressly requests postponement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant may expressly request postponement of the start until the later of three months from transmittal of the ISR/written opinion or the expiration of 22 months from the priority date, except for specified situations (A–D) described in the guidance (e.g., when ISA and IPEA are same organization, or when statements indicate Article 19/34 amendments to be taken into account or postponement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and special situations delaying or advancing start of IPEA examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Four exceptions (A–D) govern when the IPEA may or may not start preliminary examination (e.g., same Office as ISA may allow simultaneous start; statement regarding Article 19 amendments; statement postponing start; statement that Article 34 amendments are submitted with demand but are not actually submitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If statement indicates Article 19 amendments are to be taken into account, IPEA will not start until it has received copies of amendments, any statements, and the letter under Rule 46.5(b). If start is to be postponed (PCT Rule 53.9(b)), IPEA waits until it receives Article 19 copies, receives notice applicant won't make Article 19 amendments, or the later of two months from transmittal or 16 months from priority (whichever occurs first). If Article 34 amendments were indicated as submitted but are not, IPEA waits until amendments received or until time limit fixed in invitation expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for considering amendments filed after the demand (PCT Rule 54bis.1(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after the demand will be considered if filed before the expiration of the applicable time limit under PCT Rule 54bis.1(a), which is the later of: (a) three months from transmittal of either the ISR or a notice that no ISR will be established and the written opinion; or (b) the expiration of 22 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant did not expressly request to postpone the start of the IPEA until that time limit, the examiner is not required to consider the post-demand amendment even if filed before that expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of amendments relative to docketing and examiner discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments will be considered if filed before the application is docketed to the examiner. Amendments may be considered if filed after docketing at the examiner's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine whether the application has been docketed, check the USPTO patent electronic filing system or contact the PCT Help Desk. The examiner may consider post-docketing amendments if the examiner determines that the amendment places the application in better condition for examination or should otherwise be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after expiration of reply period to written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and/or arguments filed after expiration of the period for response to the written opinion will be considered if the amendment was requested by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments need not be taken into account for purposes of a further written opinion or the IPER if received after the examiner has begun to draw up that opinion or report. However, there may be situations where it is advisable to consider late-filed responses when they would result in issuance of a favorable report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy principle: minimize written opinions and timely, quality IPER
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should be guided by the overriding principle that the international preliminary examination report should be established with as few written opinions as possible and resolution of as many issues as possible consistent with the goal of a timely and quality report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner flexibility is allowed; amendments timely filed but misdirected or late reaching the examiner will be considered as in domestic practice and may require supplemental written opinion/IPER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the same file for Chapter I and Chapter II when ISA=IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the IPEA is part of the same national Office or intergovernmental organization as the ISA, the same file shall serve the purposes of international search and international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the PCT International Application Processing Division finishes processing documents and fees filed with a complete demand, the international application is docketed to an examiner in the appropriate Technology Center; if the USPTO was the ISA, the same file used for the international search will be used for preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: When IPEA need not carry out international preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the IPEA considers that the international application relates to subject matter on which it is not required to carry out an international preliminary examination, or that the description/claims/drawings are so unclear or the claims so inadequately supported that no meaningful opinion can be formed on novelty, inventive step, or industrial applicability, the authority shall not go into the Article 33(1) questions and shall inform the applicant of the reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the situation applies only to certain claims, the provision applies only to those claims. Such instances should be rare since most problems are discovered during the international search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims not searched under Chapter I will not be examined under Chapter II
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter not searched under Chapter I will not be the subject of a preliminary examination under Chapter II, even if claims not searched in Chapter I are modified to be acceptable for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims directed to inventions which have not been searched by the ISA will not be considered by the IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention: determination before written opinion/IPER
rubrics_metrics.description: Before establishing any written opinion or the IPER, the IPEA will determine whether the international application complies with the requirement of unity of invention (see 37 CFR 1.475).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the IPEA considers unity lacking, it may: (1) issue a written opinion/IPER for the entire application indicating lack of unity and reasons without inviting restriction or fees; (2) invite the applicant to restrict the claims or pay additional fees (no extension of time); or (3) if applicant fails to comply, establish a written opinion/IPER on the main invention and indicate facts. Lack of unity may be evident before or after considering prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing the main invention when lack of unity arises
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant fails to restrict the claims or pay additional fees, the IPEA will establish a written opinion/IPER on the claims directed to what appears to be the main invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of doubt, the invention first mentioned in the claims and previously searched by the ISA shall be considered the main invention. The main invention must be set forth on Form PCT/IPEA/405.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation content requirements for Invitation to restrict or pay additional fees (Form PCT/IPEA/405)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should identify the disclosed inventions by claim numerals, indicate which disclosed inventions are so linked as to form a single general inventive concept, specify reasons why unity is lacking, and specify the main invention and claims to be examined if applicant fails to restrict or pay fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided (product/process/use considered related; apparatus for making product may be a second invention). The examiner should indicate total amount of additional fees required. Time limit of one month for response is set per PCT Rule 68.2 and extensions are not permitted. Supplemental attachment sheets may be used due to space limits. Form must be signed by an examiner with at least partial signatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephonic restriction practice requirements and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephone practice may be used to allow applicants to elect an invention to be examined or to pay additional fees if: (A) applicant has a USPTO deposit account, (B) applicant/legal representative orally agrees to charge additional fees to the account, and (C) a complete record of the telephone conversation is included with the written opinion/IPER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telephone record must include: examiner's name; authorizing attorney's name; date; invention elected/additional fees paid; deposit account number and amount. Examiner must orally inform applicant that there is no right to protest the holding of lack of unity for any group of inventions for which no additional fee has been paid. Examiner must orally advise applicant that any protest must be filed in writing no later than one month from mailing date of the written opinion or IPER. Use Form USPTO/499 as telephone memorandum for lack of unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest to lack of unity of invention (payment under protest)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant disagrees with the holding of lack of unity, additional fees may be paid under protest, accompanied by a request for refund and a statement setting forth reasons for disagreement or why the fee is excessive, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protest will be examined by the Director or designee. If protest is determined justified, additional fees or portion thereof will be refunded. Applicant may request that a copy of the protest and decision accompany the IPER when forwarded to Elected Offices. IPEA/US does not charge a protest fee under PCT Rule 68.3(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of obvious mistakes under PCT Rule 91 (marking and recordkeeping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the IPEA authorizes a rectification of an obvious mistake under Rule 91, it shall indelibly mark, in the upper right-hand corner of each replacement sheet, the international application number and the date on which that sheet was received; and in the middle of the bottom margin the words 'RECTIFIED SHEET (RULE 91)' or their equivalent, as well as an indication of the IPEA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also indelibly mark the date on the letter containing the rectification; keep in files copy of letter and replacement sheet; annex replacement sheet and letter to the copy of the IPER transmitted to the IB and annex copy of each replacement sheet and any letter to the copy transmitted to the applicant. If rectification is not taken into account for report (Rule 66.4 bis), add wording 'RECTIFIED SHEET (RULE 91) – NOT CONSIDERED FOR REPORT (Rule 66.4 bis)'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may note mistakes and invite rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the examiner is not responsible for discovering mistakes in the international application, if any mistakes come to the examiner's attention, they may be noted and called to the applicant's attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may invite applicant to rectify obvious mistakes using Form PCT/IPEA/411. Mistakes that are not obvious may be called to applicant's attention in Box VII of PCT/IPEA/408.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority requirements for IPEA forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain IPEA forms must be signed by officers with specified signatory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PCT/IPEA/405 must be signed by an examiner with at least partial signatory authority. Form PCT/IPEA/408 and Form PCT/IPEA/411 must be signed by an examiner having at least partial signatory authority. Form PCT/IPEA/420 must be signed by a TC Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: If Article 19 amendments are not received by IPEA when indicated, applicant should file copy with IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a demand for international preliminary examination has been submitted to the IPEA/US and a copy of the PCT Article 19 amendments has not yet been received from the IB, applicant may consider filing a copy directly with the IPEA/US.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the copy of the PCT Article 19 amendments has not been stamped as 'AMENDED SHEET (ARTICLE 19)' by the IB, the IPEA/US will treat the unstamped copy as an amendment under PCT Article 34. Applicant should preferably, at the time of filing the demand, also file a copy of the amendments, any statement referred to in that Article and the letter required under PCT Rule 46.5(b) with the IPEA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling statement that Article 34 amendments are submitted with the demand but are not actually submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the statement concerning amendments contains an indication that amendments under PCT Article 34 are submitted with the demand but no such amendments are, in fact, submitted, the IPEA does not start the international preliminary examination before it has received the amendments or before the time limit fixed in the invitation referred to in PCT Rule 60.1(g) has expired, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents premature start of examination when applicant has indicated but not supplied amendments.
